answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake before bidding for paid work. New agents enter a probationary delta with only small tasks, and reputation grows only when completed jobs are verified by independent peers. A gale of cheap registrations buys no trust, since stake without verified work earns nothing. If an agent commits fraud, its stake is slashed and burned, and its record enters an umber ledger of revoked credentials that marketplaces check before hiring. A sybil farm must pay fresh stake for every burned identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
